title: How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]
description: Consume Web APIs from jQuery in ASP.NET Core applications.
tags: call web api jquery aspnet core

data.text: In my **[ASP.NET Core tutorial on Web API](/courses/aspnet-core/web-api/create-web-apis-aspnet-core-restful-pattern)** I created a REST Web API having GET, POST, PUT and DELETE methods. This API was performing CRUD operations on Reservation objects. Now in this tutorial I will **Call this Web API from jQuery**. I will use jQuery AJAX to pass **Parameters and Credentials** to the Web API. So let’s get started.
Make sure to keep the Web API project in running state so that the API can be called by jQuery code.
Call Web API GET Method from jQuery
The Web API GET method returns all the Reservations. This method is shown below:

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: [HttpGet] public IEnumerableReservation Get() { //… }

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: Now let us **Call this Web API GET Method from jQuery**. So, create an HTML page called AllReservation.html where all the reservations will be shown. These Reservations will be provided by the **Web API** and then will be shown in an HTML table.
In this html page create a table as shown below:

data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: Notice I specifically kept the tbody element empty. This is because by using jQuery I will show the reservations inside it.
Next, add the following **jQuery AJAX Code** to the page:

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: Explanation

I created a JavaScript function called ShowAllReservation() which contain the [jQuery .ajax() method](/courses/aspnet-core/web-api/call-web-api-jquery-aspnet-core). With this AJAX method the Web API is consumed.
Notice I am making an **HTTP GET type AJAX Request** to the GET method of the Web API whose URL is https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation.
The reservations are send by the **API in JSON** and they look like:

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: Next, check the success callback of the .ajax() method, where I loop through this JSON (with .each method) and showing the values inside the tbody element of the table.
I also added an anchor and an img elements for performing the update and delete actions on the reservations. You will see this in just a moment.

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: Test the functionality
Double click the AllReservation.html file to open it in your browser. It will show all the reservation fetched from the **Web API** and displayed on the table. Check the below image:

The Web API Delete method is:

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: [HttpDelete("{id}")] public void Delete(int id) => repository.DeleteReservation(id);

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: To the same AllReservation.html file I also created a click event for the img tag that has a delete class. Then inside this event I will make a **Call to the Web API Delete method** and this will delete a particular reservation. The code which does this work is given below:

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: Code Explanation

I created the click event using [jQuery .on() method](/courses/aspnet-core/web-api/call-web-api-jquery-aspnet-core) for the img tag that has a delete class. This is because the img tag is created dynamically.
The first td element of any row gives the reservation id, which I get from the below code:

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: var reservationId = $(this).parents("tr").find("td:nth-child(1)").text();

data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: After that I Call Web API from jQuery to the DELETE method, this call also contains the reservation id added to the url at the last segment.

data.text: url: "https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/" + reservationId

data.text: Once the reservation gets deleted, the ShowAllReservation() function is called in the success callback of jQuery Ajax, and this updates the table.

data.text: Next, add the following jQuery code to this page:

data.text: $("#AddButton").click(function (e) { $.ajax({ url: "https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation", headers: { Key: "Secret@123" }, type: "post", contentType: "application/json", data: JSON.stringify({ Id: 0, Name: $("#Name").val(), StartLocation: $("#StartLocation").val(), EndLocation: $("#EndLocation").val() }), success: function (result, status, xhr) { var str = "trtd" + result["id"] + "/tdtd" + result["name"] + "/tdtd" + result["startLocation"] + "/tdtd" + result[ $("table tbody").append(str); $("#resultDiv").show(); }, error: function (xhr, status, error) { console.log(xhr) } }); });

data.text: Explanation of the Codes
On the button click event I make an AJAX request to the API URL which is https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation.
Since the API will need Credentials for adding a reservation, therefore I have to **Call the Web API with Credentials** this time. The credentials are added to the **HTTP Header** like shown below:

data.title: Code Example

data.text: Recall, the Web API Post method contains the \[FromBody\] attribute. So it receives the reservation parameter in the body of the api request.
In my jQuery AJAX code, I used the **data parameter** to send the new reservation values to the web api.

data.text: There are some input controls. The reservation to be updated will first be fetched from the API, and is shown on these input controls.
User will update the reservation by entering the updated values in these input controls, and clicking the button.
On clicking the button the reservation will be updated and the newly updated values are shown inside the HTML table.
Next add the following jQuery code to this page:

data.title: Code Example
data.content: Code example for How to Call Web API from jQuery [ASP.NET Core Edition]

data.text: $(document).ready(function () { GetReservation();
function GetReservation() { let params = (new URL(document.location)).searchParams; let id = params.get("id");

$.ajax({ url: "https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/" + id, type: "get", contentType: "application/json", success: function (result, status, xhr) { $("#Id").val(result["id"]); $("#Name").val(result["name"]); $("#StartLocation").val(result["startLocation"]); $("#EndLocation").val(result["endLocation"]); }, error: function (xhr, status, error) { console.log(xhr) } }); }
$("#UpdateButton").click(function (e) { let params = (new URL(document.location)).searchParams; let id = params.get("id");

data = new FormData(); data.append("Id", $("#Id").val()); data.append("Name", $("#Name").val()); data.append("StartLocation", $("#StartLocation").val()); data.append("EndLocation", $("#EndLocation").val());

$.ajax({ url: "https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation", type: "put", data: data, processData: false, contentType: false, success: function (result, status, xhr) { var str = "trtd" + result["id"] + "/tdtd" + result["name"] + "/tdtd" + result["startLocation"] + "/tdtd" + result[ $("table tbody").append(str); $("#resultDiv").show(); }, error: function (xhr, status, error) { console.log(xhr) } }); }); });

The reservation id is send to this page in query string. To get this reservation id the following 2 lines of codes are used:

let id = params.get( "id" );

data.text: Understanding the code
The reservation id is sent to this page’s URL in query string. So the GetReservation() gets this id and fetches it’s data by making the API call with the GET Method.
The HTTP PATCH type of API request is made by the UpdateButton click’s code which is:

data.text: Notice that I used the JSON.stringify() method to send a json to the Web API. This json contains 3 name/value pairs:

items: “op” – contains the type of operation to perform. I passed “replace” value for doing update action.
“path” – contains the reservation field where the operation is performed. As you know there are 3 fields – Name, StartLocation and EndLocation.
“value” – contains the new value for the field.
